It takes real courage to name this and to decide you want it to stop—that's a meaningful first step, and I'm glad you're looking for a way forward.

Sometimes scratching happens almost automatically, especially when tension or difficult feelings build up. A few things can help: keeping your hands busy with something like a stress ball, holding ice, or applying lotion when you notice the urge; keeping your nails short; and paying attention to what tends to come right before it, so you can catch the pattern earlier.

That said, this is something you deserve real support with. Talking to a doctor or counselor can help you understand what's driving it and build tools that actually last. If you ever feel like you might seriously hurt yourself, please reach out to a crisis line or emergency services right away—you can call or text 988 in the US.

Would it help to think through who you might talk to first?
